transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because I've been having this problem when I try to talk to people. When someone asks me a really simple question at work—like when a ring repair will be ready—my answer just starts wandering all over the place. 

I'll start off fine, but then I'm suddenly jumping from the store invoices to... garden soil, or my mortgage papers. I can just look at their faces and see that they're completely losing me. It's just getting really hard to give a straight answer, and I need to figure out why it's happening.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, taken out of your mind, or broadcasted so others can hear them?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. My thoughts are definitely my own. They just get... well, tangled up when I try to say them out loud. But nobody is putting them in my head or taking them away, and I definitely don't think anyone can hear what I'm thinking.
Have you ever experienced any strange or unusual perceptions, like hearing voices when no one is around, or seeing things that others don't see?

Well, yes, actually. Sometimes when the shop is quiet, I'll hear a woman mutter my name... it sounds like it's coming from the polishing room, even when I know I'm the only one there. And sometimes I'll smell burning metal, like someone left a torch on, but I know the torches are off. It always feels real enough that I actually get up and go check the back room just to be sure. But I haven't seen anything that isn't there, it's just the sounds and the smells.

latest_inference.note: The patient reported experiencing auditory and olfactory hallucinations (e.g., hearing a woman's voice mutter their name and smelling burning metal), which are significant indicators of a psychotic disorder. The absence of thought insertion, withdrawal, or broadcasting rules out schizophrenia (F20.x) and supports the diagnosis of acute polymorphic psychotic disorder without symptoms of schizophrenia (F23.1).
